docs.title: gpkvt/pyinfra
docs.text:
This repository contains a pyinfra deployment configuration for Debian and Ubuntu systems. It includes inventory, host and group data, deployment entry points, reusable task modules, templates, files and scripts.

It uses the separate upstream pyinfra automation tool to execute operations on local and remote machines. This repository is deployment code; it is not the upstream pyinfra engine.

docs.title: Repository contents
docs.text:
Area What it manages Documentation System Packages, users, SSH, host configuration, storage and services Task reference Docker Compose applications, persistent data, systemd user services and integrations Docker guide Network VPN, Samba, Syncthing, firewall and proxy-related services Task overview Workstation COSMIC, Flatpak, power management, hardware and desktop tools Feature reference Configuration Inventory, host/group data, feature flags and encrypted credentials Configuration

Optional features are selected through deployment code and host or group data. They are not all enabled on every target.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or newer for the project environment.
  • Debian or Ubuntu target systems, as configured by this repository.
  • SSH access and suitable privileges for remote deployments.
  • Docker Engine and the Compose plugin for Docker tasks.

See development for the project environment and configuration for inventory and host data.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
Install the Python environment, review the inventory and host data, then preview the deployment:

uv sync
pyinfra inventory.py deploy.py --dry --diff

Review the proposed operations before applying them:

pyinfra inventory.py deploy.py --diff

A dry run is a review step, not a substitute for backups or testing. Some tasks modify networking, firewall rules, authentication or running services and can interrupt access.

docs.title: Docker storage and lifecycle
docs.text:
Docker tasks are opt-in through the docker host-data configuration. The repository uses these conventions:

  • Compose project files and persistent application data are stored below ~/.docker/<service>/ for the configured user.
  • Persistent application data uses host bind mounts. Docker-managed named volumes are not used.
  • Web interfaces bind to loopback by default where applicable.
  • systemd user units manage Compose project lifecycle.
  • Credentials are read from the configured encrypted secrets source where supported.

The Docker guide documents the service catalog, ports, storage paths, prerequisites and service-specific settings.

docs.title: Upstream pyinfra
docs.text:
Upstream pyinfra is maintained separately at pyinfra-dev/pyinfra. It provides the automation engine, inventory handling, facts, operations and connectors used by this repository.

See Upstream pyinfra for the relationship between the engine and this deployment repository, and links to the upstream documentation.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
HOW THE PROJECT FITS TOGETHER

Understand how inventory, host data, deployment logic and task modules work together to produce repeatable infrastructure changes.

InventoryWhere pyinfra connects Host dataWhat each machine needs TasksHow changes are applied

This project uses pyinfra to turn Python host data into repeatable infrastructure operations. Its main separation is between where to connect, what a host should look like, and how to implement each change.

docs.title: Repository layers
docs.text:
inventory.py ─────── target names, SSH options and privilege escalation
       │
       ▼
group_data/ ──────── per-host desired configuration (host.data)
       │
       ▼
deploy.py ────────── initialization and conditional task selection
       │
       ▼
tasks/*.py ───────── pyinfra operations and task-specific validation
       │             ├── templates/  rendered, parameterized files
       │             └── files/      static payloads
       ▲
common.py ────────── shared runtime values and decrypted secrets
Component Responsibility inventory.py Declares target hosts, SSH connection settings and _sudo behavior. group_data/ Supplies target-specific and group/role settings, exposed together through host.data. deploy.py Calls initialization, includes core tasks and gates optional tasks. common.py Loads the encrypted secrets file and publishes shared runtime values. tasks/ Declares operations for system, network, service and user configuration. templates/ Holds Jinja2 templates rendered by task modules. files/ Holds static files copied or synchronized by task modules, including the gpg-vault secret-management utility.

docs.title: Execution lifecycle
docs.text:
1. Inventory loading. pyinfra loads inventory.py. production is built from _all_hosts after removing names in disabled_hosts. The special @local host represents the machine running pyinfra.
  2. Initialization. deploy.py calls common.initialize(host, check_flatpak=True). The function checks for secrets.json.gpg; when present, it runs gpg --decrypt, parses JSON, and assigns the result to builtins.secrets. If absent, it assigns an empty dictionary. It also sets builtins.homedir and, when requested, builtins.flatpak from the Which fact.
  3. Task selection. Core task modules are included unconditionally. Optional modules are included when the relevant host.data value, secret entry, or detected executable is truthy. The workstation role is an inventory group: workstation = ["@local"] assigns the local target to that group, and pyinfra loads group_data/workstation.py alongside the host's own data. deploy.py then includes each tasks/workstation/*.py module only when its matching workstation.<feature>.enabled setting is true. The exact gates are listed in Deployment workflow.
  4. Local secret maintenance. files/scripts/gpg-vault is synchronized to the configured user's scripts directory by tasks/scripts.py and linked into /usr/local/bin/. It is an operator-facing tool; common.initialize() continues to decrypt secrets.json.gpg itself during deployment.
  5. Operation execution. pyinfra prepares operations by reading facts and determining the required changes, then executes them in order. Facts read directly in deploy code describe the pre-deployment state; use operation callbacks such as did_change and any_changed through _if when a later operation depends on an earlier operation's result. Never branch on an operation's change result with an ordinary Python if during preparation.

docs.title: Host and group data
docs.text: Values in group_data/<host>.py and matching group-data files are exposed through host.data. A target can therefore receive both its host-specific settings and shared role settings. For example, workstation = ["@local"] in inventory.py assigns @local to the workstation group, whose settings are defined in group_data/workstation.py. Tasks access these values with host.data.<name> or host.data.get(<name>, default). Existing host settings include apt_packages, wireguard_config, docker, ufw, and zsh; workstation role settings are nested under host.data.workstation.

docs.title: Shared builtins
docs.text:
common.initialize() currently publishes:

Name Meaning secrets Parsed decrypted JSON dictionary, or {} if no encrypted file is found. homedir host.data.homedir, defaulting to /root/. flatpak Result of the Flatpak Which fact when check_flatpak=True.

Some task modules initialize common themselves when homedir has not yet been set. Avoid adding new implicit globals; prefer explicit task inputs where practical.

docs.title: Task organization
docs.text:
Tasks are grouped by responsibility rather than by host. General tasks live directly under tasks/; optional workstation-role tasks are grouped under tasks/workstation/. deploy.py owns orchestration and should remain the authoritative place for full-deployment feature gates. A task module should:

  • Read only the host data and secrets it needs.
  • Validate user-controlled configuration before creating operations where appropriate.
  • Keep file ownership and permissions explicit.
  • Avoid overwriting user-generated material unless that behavior is intentional and documented.
  • Be safe to run repeatedly and use pyinfra facts/conditions to minimize unnecessary changes.

docs.title: Docker lifecycle
docs.text:
Docker Compose projects, generated environment files and persistent host data live below `~/.docker//`. Each project is managed by a user-level systemd unit whose working directory is that service directory. Persistent data uses explicit host bind mounts; Docker-managed named volumes are not used.

Keep Compose lifecycle commands behind the shared systemd helper. Replacing this flow with pyinfra's stateless `docker.compose` operation would bypass the user-level unit and Sablier preparation/restart rules. The helper instead gates image pulls, container reconciliation and systemd restarts on actual configuration changes.

docs.title: Templates and static assets
docs.text: Use templates/ when a file needs host-specific values or secrets at render time. Use files/ for static content. A task is responsible for choosing the destination, owner, group, mode and reload/restart behavior. See Templates and static files.

docs.title: Important boundaries
docs.text:
• A task being present in the repository does not mean it is automatically deployed; deploy.py controls inclusion.
  • Secret availability and host configuration are separate conditions. WireGuard, for example, needs both a host-side interface definition and matching secret data.
  • The WireGuard task writes configuration but does not start the tunnel. The VPN task manages the wg-quick@... service based on IPv4 network detection.
  • The local target can change the machine executing pyinfra. Treat @local with the same care as a production host.

docs.title: Host configuration
docs.text:
DEFINE THE DESIRED STATE

Configure each machine with tracked examples and private local data. Keep feature choices readable, credentials protected and task logic reusable.

group_data/Host and role settings workstationOpt-in desktop features secretsEncrypted credentials

Host-specific desired state is stored as Python data in group_data/. pyinfra exposes the values for a target through host.data. Real machine configuration is intentionally untracked: .gitignore excludes group_data/@local.py and group_data/workstation.py. The repository tracks portable templates at group_data/@local.py.example and group_data/workstation.py.example instead.

After cloning, create local copies before deploying:

cp group_data/@local.py.example group_data/@local.py
cp group_data/workstation.py.example group_data/workstation.py

Edit both files for the target machine. Replace every identity placeholder, verify hardware and network settings, and explicitly enable only the workstation features required on that host. Keep credentials, private keys, USB device rules, real hostnames, IP addresses and other machine-specific data in the ignored local files. Do not force-add these files to Git.

docs.title: Which files are used?
docs.text:
The inventory target name determines its host-data file: the local target uses the ignored group_data/@local.py, and a target named web01 uses group_data/web01.py. Inventory groups can add shared configuration for a role or class of hosts. For example, workstation = ["@local"] in inventory.py makes @local a member of the workstation group, so pyinfra also loads the ignored group_data/workstation.py. Group data and host data are both available through host.data; keep role-wide defaults in the workstation file and host-specific overrides in the local file.

The workstation group is optional. Add a host to the workstation inventory group only if it should receive that role's configuration and eligible workstation tasks.

Keep configuration data separate from task logic. Put private keys, passwords, API tokens and credential-bearing URLs in the encrypted secrets file, not in group data. Use the deployed gpg-vault command to manage that file without routinely handling plaintext manually. See Secrets management.

docs.title: Common settings
docs.text:
Setting Purpose Notes hostname System hostname Managed by tasks/system.py. username Primary user Used by user-scoped tasks; some tasks default to root if omitted. usergroup Primary group Used by user-scoped tasks; some tasks default to root. homedir User home directory Also published as builtins.homedir; defaults to /root/ in common.initialize(). timezone System timezone Use a valid zoneinfo identifier. locale System locale Defaults to en_US.UTF-8 in the system task; set to None to skip locale management. keyboard XKB keyboard configuration Empty dictionary disables management. editor / visual_editor Default editors visual_editor falls back to editor.

Example:

hostname = "workstation"
username = "deploy"
usergroup = "deploy"
homedir = "/home/deploy"
timezone = "Etc/UTC"
locale = "en_US.UTF-8"
editor = "vim"

docs.title: Workstation role
docs.text:
The tracked group_data/workstation.py.example defines a shared, nested workstation configuration. Copy it to the ignored group_data/workstation.py and edit it locally. deploy.py checks each feature's enabled flag and includes its corresponding task only when that flag is true. The example disables every feature until explicitly enabled.

Setting Default in tracked example Effect workstation.backup.enabled False Installs Restic, Borg, rsync and Borgmatic, and renders /etc/borgmatic/config.yaml. It does not create or run a backup job; repository locations, credentials, sources, retention and restore testing still need configuration. workstation.power.enabled False Installs and enables the selected power manager. manager must be tlp or power-profiles-daemon; the other manager is removed. workstation.hardware.enabled False Installs fwupd and, when selected, CPU microcode (intel or amd). Firmware updates are not applied automatically. workstation.storage.enabled False Installs smartmontools and nvme-cli; no monitoring schedule or alerting is configured. workstation.peripherals.enabled False Enables optional printer/scanner support. Set printing and/or scanning to true; CUPS is enabled when printing is selected. workstation.desktop.enabled False Installs common desktop integration utilities. packages can replace the default package list. workstation.maintenance.enabled False Installs needrestart, debian-goodies and apt-file; no unattended upgrades or automatic reboots are enabled.

Example role configuration:

workstation = {
    "backup": {"enabled": True},
    "power": {"enabled": True, "manager": "tlp"},
    "hardware": {"enabled": True, "cpu_vendor": "amd"},
    "storage": {"enabled": True},
    "peripherals": {
        "enabled": False,
        "printing": False,
        "scanning": False,
    },
    "desktop": {"enabled": False},
    "maintenance": {"enabled": False},
}

COSMIC configuration is nested exclusively under workstation.cosmic; do not define a separate top-level cosmic variable in per-host data. The COSMIC deployment includes independently gated appearance, window management, input, shortcuts, panel, dock and workspace modules. Display/output settings are intentionally excluded.

Optional custom COSMIC configuration directories can be synchronized with workstation.cosmic.config_files. Each entry is a mapping with a repository-relative src directory and a destination dest relative to the configured user's home directory:

workstation = {
    "cosmic": {
        "enabled": True,
        "config_files": {
            "appearance": {
                "src": "files/cosmic/local/appearance/",
                "dest": ".config/cosmic/com.system76.CosmicTheme.Mode/v1/",
            },
            "panel": {
                "src": "files/cosmic/local/panel/",
                "dest": ".config/cosmic/com.system76.CosmicPanel.Panel/v1/",
            },
            "dock": {
                "src": "files/cosmic/local/dock/",
                "dest": ".config/cosmic/com.system76.CosmicPanel.Dock/v1/",
            },
        },
    },
}

The source directories are synchronized as supplied, with files owned by the configured user and group. Keep machine-specific files and secrets out of tracked source directories. Do not put display/output configuration in these directories if the goal is to keep display layouts machine-specific.

The tracked workstation example disables all features by default. Review each feature's requirements before enabling it. In particular, the backup task only installs tools and deploys a Borgmatic configuration template; it does not configure repository credentials or schedule backups. The current Borgmatic template also contains a literal fallback encryption passphrase (B0rgm4t1C!) and the generated file is mode 0600; do not use that fallback for real backups. See Templates and static assets for the security caveat.

docs.title: Network and name resolution
docs.text:
hostnames maps IP addresses to one or more hostnames and is consumed by tasks/hosts.py to manage /etc/hosts.

hostnames = {
    "127.0.0.1": ["localhost"],
    "::1": ["localhost"],
    "192.0.2.10": ["app.example.test", "app"],
}

Each IP address must map to a list; space-separated strings are no longer accepted. Convert an old value such as "app.example.test app" to ["app.example.test", "app"]. An empty list removes all entries for that IP address from /etc/hosts.

VPN-related settings:

Setting Purpose local_network_cidr IPv4 CIDR used to detect whether the host is on the trusted/local network. wireguard_interface Interface name used by the VPN service task. wireguard_config Mapping of interface names to WireGuard interface settings.

The VPN task currently checks globally scoped IPv4 addresses only. It starts/enables wg-quick@<wireguard_interface> when none belongs to the configured local CIDR. It does not evaluate IPv6 network membership.

docs.title: Packages and repositories
docs.text:
• apt_packages: list of Debian package names installed by tasks/apt.py.
  • apt_sources: mapping of repository identifiers to signing-key and APT source definitions. The task uses apt.key to install/dearmor signing keys and creates .list source files. Keyring paths must end in .gpg and must match each repository's signed-by option.
  • flatpak_packages: list of Flatpak application IDs. tasks/flatpak.py is included only when the Flatpak executable is detected. Flatpak installations and updates retry failures three times with five seconds between retries, then allow the remaining deployment tasks to continue if the remote remains unavailable. Errors remain visible; unsuccessful packages are not considered installed and must be retried later.

Example:

apt_packages = ["curl", "git", "rsync"]
flatpak_packages = ["org.mozilla.firefox"]

Review third-party repository URLs, distributions, architectures and signing-key sources before enabling them.

docs.title: System hardening and access
docs.text:
Setting Consumed by Purpose sysctl tasks/system.py Kernel parameters, applied immediately and persisted in /etc/sysctl.d/99-local.conf. udev tasks/system.py Mapping of .rules filenames to rule contents. usbguard tasks/system.py Daemon policy and explicit device authorization rules. sudoers_rules tasks/sudo.py Custom sudoers lines installed after visudo validation. ssh_keys tasks/ssh_keys.py SSH keypair definitions to generate when absent. ssh_authorized_keys tasks/ssh_keys.py Mapping of users to authorized public keys. ssh_config tasks/ssh_config.py SSH client configuration rendered from a template. apparmor_profiles tasks/apparmor.py Profiles to enforce.

For detailed validation, file paths and safety considerations, see System configuration and Task reference.

docs.title: Optional user and desktop features
docs.text:
Setting Module Expected content zsh tasks/zsh.py Truthy enablement value; includes the Zsh dotfiles and generates .zshrc. zshrc_imports tasks/zsh.py Optional list of additional Zsh configuration files or import statements inserted into the generated .zshrc; defaults to an empty list. zplug_plugins tasks/zsh.py Optional list of zplug plugin definitions; defaults to an empty list. tmux tasks/tmux.py Truthy enablement value. powerline tasks/powerline.py Truthy enablement value. powerline_fonts tasks/fonts.py Boolean-like flag for optional patched fonts. workstation.cosmic tasks/workstation/cosmic/deploy.py COSMIC desktop settings, enabled only through the workstation role. Display/output settings are deliberately excluded. workstation.cosmic.window_management tasks/workstation/cosmic/window_management.py Optional autotile, autotile_behavior (PerWorkspace or Global), focus_follows_cursor, cursor_follows_focus, edge_snap_threshold value. workstation.cosmic.input tasks/workstation/cosmic/input.py Optional raw COSMIC RON strings for default (mouse) and touchpad; hardware-specific settings must be supplied explicitly. workstation.cosmic.shortcuts tasks/workstation/cosmic/shortcuts.py Optional raw RON map for com.system76.CosmicSettings.Shortcuts/v1/custom. vscodium tasks/vscodium.py Extension configuration dictionary. mullvad_extensions tasks/mullvad_extensions.py Extension IDs and download URLs. mullvad_browser_dir tasks/mullvad_extensions.py Browser distribution directory; task default is /usr/lib/mullvad-browser/distribution. proton tasks/proton.py Proton application selection and options.

When Proton Drive CLI installation is enabled, set proton.drive_cli_version explicitly to the release to install. There is no fallback version.

Example:

zsh = True
zshrc_imports = [
    "source ~/.config/zsh/local.zsh",
    "source ~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh",
]
zplug_plugins = ["zsh-users/zsh-autosuggestions", "zsh-users/zsh-syntax-highlighting"]

zshrc_imports entries are rendered into the generated .zshrc; ensure referenced files exist for the configured user. Keep credentials out of these files unless they are protected separately.

docs.title: On-demand Samba file exchange
docs.text:
The optional top-level samba mapping enables a guest-accessible LAN/VPN file exchange server. It provides a shared writable Upload dropbox and a read-only Download share. The task installs and configures Samba but leaves smbd stopped and masked; use the deployed samba-start and samba-stop commands to open/close TCP 445 in UFW and start/stop the service. Configure trusted CIDRs explicitly. Upload guests share one Unix identity and can manage one another's files; this is a convenience dropbox, not private per-device storage. See Samba documentation for the full configuration and security model.

Example:

samba = {
    "enabled": True,
    "interface": "enp3s0",
    "allowed_networks": ["192.168.1.0/24"],
    "idle_timeout": 3600,  # 0 disables automatic shutdown
    "upload": {"path": "/srv/samba/upload"},
    "download": {"path": "/srv/samba/download"},
}

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
docker is a mapping of service names to service-specific settings. The supported keys are adguard_home, appflowy, miniflux, timetagger, grav, forgejo, portainer, tasmoadmin, wallabag, vaultwarden, nocodb, linkwarden, homepage, paperless, firefly-iii, snipe-it, mdmesh and wg-easy. Each service has its own options; inspect its module under tasks/docker/ and its Compose template under templates/docker/<service>/ before adding keys.

All current services persist application data through host bind mounts below the configured user's home directory:

Service Persistent host path Default loopback port Miniflux ~/.docker/miniflux/db/ (PostgreSQL database) 8080 TimeTagger ~/.docker/timetagger/ 8080 Grav ~/.docker/grav/data/ 8080 Forgejo ~/.docker/forgejo/data/ 8027 (HTTP), 2222 (SSH) Portainer ~/.docker/portainer/data/ 9000 TasmoAdmin ~/.docker/tasmoadmin/data/ 8016 Wallabag ~/.docker/wallabag/data/, ~/.docker/wallabag/images/ 8017 Vaultwarden ~/.docker/vaultwarden/ 8018 NocoDB ~/.docker/nocodb/data/ 8019 Homepage ~/.docker/homepage/config/ 8020 Paperless-ngx ~/.docker/paperless/postgres/, data/, media/, consume/, export/ 8022 Linkwarden ~/.docker/linkwarden/postgres/, data/, meili/ 8021 Firefly III ~/.docker/firefly-iii/database/, upload/, fints/ 8023 (FinTS importer: 8024) Snipe-IT ~/.docker/snipe-it/database/, storage/ 8025 AppFlowy ~/.docker/appflowy/postgres/, minio/, search/ 8026 WG-Easy ~/.docker/wg-easy/ UI 51821; WireGuard UDP 51820

The interfaces bind to 127.0.0.1 by default, except explicitly published protocol ports such as WG-Easy WireGuard UDP. All persistent service data uses direct host bind mounts below ~/.docker/, not Docker-managed named volumes. The shared Docker helper renders Compose files under ~/.docker/<service>/ and user-level systemd units under ~/.config/systemd/user/. A changed Compose file triggers an image pull and container preparation; unchanged Compose files do not trigger a pull. User-level systemd units manage the Compose projects, while Sablier can start labelled services on demand when enabled.

Service-specific behavior:

  • AppFlowy deploys the official AppFlowy Self-Hosted Commercial Compose stack behind the existing Caddy instance. The public hostname is appflowy.21x9.org; Nginx publishes only 127.0.0.1:8026. PostgreSQL, MinIO and Search persist in ~/.docker/appflowy/postgres/, minio/ and search/ using host bind mounts. The task creates ~/.docker/appflowy/.env with mode 0600 from encrypted secrets. Configure secrets.docker.appflowy.postgres_password, admin_password, jwt_secret, minio_access_key and minio_secret_key. The initial administrator password must be at least 16 URL-safe characters. Generate the PostgreSQL password, JWT secret and MinIO secret key with openssl rand -hex 32; generate the exactly 20-character MinIO access key with openssl rand -hex 10. The first GoTrue administrator is created from docker.appflowy.admin_email (default admin@appflowy.21x9.org) and the encrypted admin_password. Change the initial password after first login. Cloud, AI, Worker and Search receive their respective Redis connection URLs from the generated environment file and connect to the Compose redis service, never container-local localhost. Redis follows the upstream ephemeral configuration and has no persistent data mount or AOF; pending queue state may not survive Redis replacement. SMTP and AI provider keys are optional and remain unset by default. AppFlowy is the commercial self-hosted distribution; review the upstream license before deployment. Homepage only links to AppFlowy and does not call its authenticated API.

  • Miniflux runs with a PostgreSQL companion container. Set docker.miniflux.postgres_version explicitly and optionally configure port; credentials are supplied through secrets.docker.miniflux. Deployment fails if the PostgreSQL version is missing or invalid.

  • TimeTagger mounts its persistent directory at the container's /root/_timetagger.
  • Grav supports image, port, channel, setup, scheduler and fix_permissions options.
  • Forgejo supports image, port, ssh_port, ssh_server and domain. HTTP and SSH bind to loopback by default. The configurable HTTP host port defaults to 8027 and maps to container port 3000. If an existing host sets docker.forgejo.port explicitly, update it and the corresponding Caddy reverse_proxy target together.
  • Portainer mounts the Docker socket, giving it administrative control over the Docker host. Keep its interface private or protect the reverse-proxy route with strong authentication.
  • TasmoAdmin mounts its data at /data/tasmoadmin inside the container, matching TASMO_DATADIR.
  • Wallabag uses SQLite, stores its database/application data and article images in the two host directories above, and disables public registration. Change the initial wallabag / wallabag account password immediately. The supplied local configuration publishes it through Caddy at wallabag.21x9.org.
  • Vaultwarden disables public signups and invitations. Its optional admin_token secret must contain an Argon2 PHC hash, generated with docker run --rm -it vaultwarden/server:latest /vaultwarden hash. The supplied local configuration publishes it through Caddy at vaultwarden.21x9.org.
  • NocoDB persists its application data in ~/.docker/nocodb/data/, mounted at /usr/app/data. It supports image, port and domain; the supplied local configuration publishes it through Caddy at nocodb.21x9.org.
  • Homepage persists its configuration in ~/.docker/homepage/config/, mounted at /app/config. It supports image, port and domain; domain is passed to HOMEPAGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS and must contain the hostname (and port, if applicable), not a URL scheme. The supplied local configuration publishes it through Caddy at homepage.21x9.org. Docker socket integration is not enabled by default. Since widgets can display sensitive data, protect the dashboard with reverse-proxy authentication, Homepage authentication, or a VPN.
  • Paperless-ngx runs PostgreSQL 17, Valkey, Gotenberg and Tika alongside the web application. PostgreSQL and Paperless application directories are mounted directly from ~/.docker/paperless/ on the host. Set uid and gid to the numeric user/group IDs that should own Paperless data (defaults to 1000:1000); PostgreSQL storage is owned by UID/GID 70:70. Configure postgres_password (URL-safe) and secret_key in secrets.docker.paperless. The web interface binds to loopback port 8022 and the supplied local Caddy hostname is paperless.21x9.org.
  • WG-Easy stores WireGuard configuration in the host bind-mounted directory ~/.docker/wg-easy/. Its web UI binds to 127.0.0.1:51821 by default and is published through Caddy at vpn.21x9.org; WireGuard listens on public UDP port 51820. The first visit opens the WG-Easy setup wizard: configure the public endpoint as vpn.21x9.org and create the administrator account there. The Compose configuration sets INSECURE=true because Caddy terminates HTTPS and proxies to the local HTTP UI. Keep the UI behind Caddy and do not expose port 51821 publicly.

Homepage configuration is managed through the docker.homepage dictionary in the host's group_data/<host>.py (for example, the ignored local copy group_data/@local.py). Each configuration area is optional and is rendered into its own YAML file:

Host-data key Generated file Purpose settings settings.yaml Dashboard title, theme, layout and global settings services services.yaml Service cards and nested service groups bookmarks bookmarks.yaml Bookmark groups and links widgets widgets.yaml Global and service widget definitions docker docker.yaml Docker integration configuration kubernetes kubernetes.yaml Kubernetes integration configuration proxmox proxmox.yaml Proxmox integration configuration

The templates serialize supplied Python dictionaries and lists as JSON, which is valid YAML. Use the structure and option names from the Homepage configuration documentation. Nested service groups and their layout can be expressed directly in host data:

docker = {
    "homepage": {
        "image": "ghcr.io/gethomepage/homepage:latest",
        "port": 8020,
        "domain": "homepage.21x9.org",
        "settings": {
            "title": "Local Dashboard",
            "layout": {
                "Infrastructure": {
                    "style": "row",
                    "columns": 3,
                    "Server": {"style": "row", "columns": 2},
                    "Network": {"style": "row", "columns": 2},
                },
            },
        },
        "services": [
            {
                "Infrastructure": [
                    {
                        "Server": [
                            {"Portainer": {
                                "href": "https://portainer.21x9.org",
                                "description": "Docker management",
                            }},
                        ],
                    },
                ],
            },
        ],
    },
}

Only keys present in docker.homepage are rendered. Omitted sections are not generated or removed; to clear a previously managed section, provide an empty list or dictionary as appropriate. The files are managed declaratively: manual edits to generated files are replaced on the next deployment.

Migration note: The current templates use host bind mounts. If a host was deployed while an earlier Wallabag or Vaultwarden template used Docker-managed named volumes, Compose does not migrate that data automatically. Back up and copy the named-volume contents into the corresponding host directory before switching. Data already present in the host directories is retained.

docker service configuration is independent of encrypted credentials. Put Miniflux credentials and the optional Vaultwarden admin-token hash in the encrypted secrets file; see Secrets management.

docs.title: Caddy and Sablier
docs.text:
Software release pins are configurable in the local host data. Set caddy_versions.version, caddy_versions.sablier_plugin, and caddy_versions.dehydrated to select the Caddy image, Sablier Caddy plugin, and Dehydrated release used to build the custom Caddy image. The Sablier server image is selected with docker_sablier.version. All four values are required when their corresponding feature is enabled; no software-version fallbacks are used. Keep these pins in group_data/@local.py (or the appropriate host/group inventory data) rather than editing task or Dockerfile sources.

caddy_config maps site addresses to Caddy directives consumed by tasks/caddy.py. Caddy is deployed inside the Docker feature gate when both docker and caddy_config are truthy. Dehydrated uses Hetzner DNS-01 credentials when at least one certificate is configured.

Migration from dehydrated_domains: move ordinary certificate names into hostnames, configure their parent zones in dehydrated_zones, and move any manually requested wildcard certificate (including its SANs) into dehydrated_wildcards. The old dehydrated_domains setting is no longer consumed. Certificate names are derived from the list-based hostnames mapping only when they are fully qualified names inside dehydrated_zones. Configure this explicit zone allowlist; no DNS lookup or IP-address classification is performed. Private, reserved and public IP addresses are treated identically, which supports NAT and split-horizon DNS. Add internal-only names or IP addresses to dehydrated_blacklist to exclude them manually. An IP entry excludes every hostname mapped to that address; a hostname entry excludes only that name. Wildcard blacklist entries match exactly one label. A wildcard certificate is an explicit request covering its entire matching namespace; configuration fails if it overlaps a blacklisted hostname.

Use dehydrated_wildcards for explicitly requested wildcard certificates, for example [["example.com", "*.example.com"]]; each inner list is one certificate and may include additional SANs. A flat list such as ["*.example.com"], an empty inner list, or another malformed entry is rejected; the error reports the offending certificate index, value and Python type to make host-data configuration mistakes easier to locate. Wildcards must fall within an allowlisted zone and suppress matching automatically derived names (one DNS label only). The dehydrated_auto_domains setting defaults to True; set it to False to disable automatic discovery entirely while retaining explicitly configured wildcard certificates. With no resulting certificate definitions, the Hetzner API token is not required and the generated Dehydrated domains file is empty. When certificates are configured, ensure secrets.dehydrated.hetzner_api_token is present and scope that token to the required Hetzner DNS zones where possible.

docker_sablier is an optional mapping. Set enabled: True to deploy Sablier before service Compose projects are prepared. The supplied local configuration uses default_duration: "10m", blocking_timeout: "10m", and stop_dependencies: True. Caddy uses the dynamic strategy by default, with default_theme: "ghost", show_details: True, and refresh_frequency: "5s"; per-service overrides live under docker.<service>.sablier. strategy: "blocking" is available for clients that cannot use the dynamic loading page. blocking_timeout applies only to blocking mode.

docker_power_save lists containers managed by the battery monitor. tasks/docker_power.py deploys the monitor and its systemd unit; the monitor is disabled while Sablier is enabled and re-enabled when Sablier is disabled. The two mechanisms are mutually exclusive.

docs.title: Syncthing
docs.text:
Set syncthing to a dictionary to install Syncthing and enable its per-user systemd service (syncthing@<username>). The task uses the top-level username setting to select the service account and configures the GUI listen address through the Syncthing CLI. The GUI defaults to loopback-only (127.0.0.1:8384); change this only when remote access is deliberately secured, for example behind an authenticated reverse proxy or VPN.

syncthing = {
    "gui_address": "127.0.0.1:8384",
}

The package creates the device identity and initial configuration on first start. Add remote devices and shared folders through the Syncthing GUI or its CLI/API; this task does not replace the generated device identity or overwrite the complete config.xml.

docs.title: Firewall
docs.text:
UFW supports the application/service keys chromecast-dlna, kdeconnect, localsend and ssh (TCP port 22), with Allow or Deny string values. It also accepts custom rules as dictionaries containing an action and a rule argument string. Custom rules are checked against ufw show added before they are applied, including normalization of UFW's optional in token, so repeated deployments do not add duplicate rules. Unsupported keys and invalid values are ignored.

For example:

ufw = {
    "ssh": "Allow",
    "kdeconnect": "Allow",
    "docker-host-https": {
        "action": "Allow",
        "rule": "in from 172.16.0.0/12 to 172.17.0.1 port 443 proto tcp",
    },
}

The task sets default incoming policy to deny and outgoing policy to allow, applies configured rules, and enables UFW. Review the effective policy and ensure an independent recovery path before applying firewall changes remotely. Set firewall policy deliberately in the ignored local host configuration; the tracked example leaves UFW configuration empty.

docs.title: Secrets-dependent configuration
docs.text:
The following features combine host data with encrypted secrets:

  • WireGuard requires wireguard_config plus matching secrets.wireguard entries.
  • Caddy's Dehydrated DNS-01 certificate workflow requires secrets.dehydrated.hetzner_api_token when Docker and caddy_config enable the Caddy task.
  • Git credentials are deployed only when secrets.git_credentials is present.
  • SSH key generation can use secrets.ssh passphrases.
  • Miniflux uses secrets.docker.miniflux for administrator and PostgreSQL credentials.
  • Paperless-ngx requires secrets.docker.paperless.postgres_password and secret_key.
  • Firefly III requires database credentials, app_key and a 32-character cron_token under secrets.docker.firefly-iii.
  • Snipe-IT requires database credentials and a persistent Laravel app_key under secrets.docker.snipe-it.
  • Linkwarden requires PostgreSQL, NextAuth and Meilisearch secrets under secrets.docker.linkwarden. The bookmark synchronizer reuses secrets.docker.homepage.environment.HOMEPAGE_VAR_LINKWARDEN_API_KEY, the same bearer token already supplied to Homepage’s Linkwarden widget; no separate token is required. The Linkwarden bookmark sync can be previewed manually from the repository root with python tasks/docker/linkwarden_bookmarks.py --dry-run; this does not download favicons or modify files. Omit --dry-run to apply the sync. The command decrypts secrets.json.gpg with GPG and reuses the Homepage API key.\n- Homepage can receive widget API keys through secrets.docker.homepage.environment; these values override matching host-data environment defaults.
  • Vaultwarden optionally uses secrets.docker.vaultwarden.admin_token for its Argon2 PHC admin-token hash.

The absence of secrets.json.gpg does not stop the whole deployment; common.initialize() sets an empty secrets dictionary. See Secrets management for the supported structure.

docs.title: Adding a host
docs.text:
1. Add a target entry to _all_hosts in inventory.py.
  2. Add its name to disabled_hosts until it is ready, if you want to prevent accidental selection through production.
  3. Create group_data/<host>.py with only the settings needed by that host.
  4. Verify SSH and privilege escalation.
  5. Run a dry deployment with a host limit and review every proposed operation.

docs.title: SSH client configuration
docs.text:
Set ssh_config to a mapping of OpenSSH Host patterns to configuration lines. The tasks/ssh_config.py task renders these entries into the configured user's ~/.ssh/config.

The generated file begins with a hardened Host * baseline that applies to all destinations:

  • HashKnownHosts yes hashes hostnames in known_hosts.
  • StrictHostKeyChecking accept-new accepts and records new host keys, but rejects changed keys.
  • UpdateHostKeys yes allows OpenSSH to learn additional host keys after a trusted connection.
  • PubkeyAuthentication yes and IdentitiesOnly yes prefer explicitly configured public-key identities.
  • ForwardAgent no, ForwardX11 no, PermitLocalCommand no and ClearAllForwardings yes disable common forwarding and local-command features.
  • ConnectTimeout 15, ServerAliveInterval 60 and ServerAliveCountMax 3 bound connection setup and detect unresponsive peers.

The baseline is intentionally rendered before custom host entries. OpenSSH uses the first obtained value for most options, so later entries cannot override these baseline values. Other per-host settings remain available:

ssh_config = {
    "github.com": """
  HostName github.com
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_github
  User git
    """,
    "192.0.2.*": """
  User deploy
  Port 2222
    """,
}

When connecting to a new host, verify its fingerprint through a trusted channel where practical. accept-new protects against changed keys, but the first connection still relies on trusting the key presented at that time.

docs.title: Deployment workflow
docs.text:
FROM REVIEW TO RECONCILIATION

Prepare a target, preview the operations and apply only the changes needed to bring it into the desired state.

PrepareInventory, data and access PreviewDry run with diffs ApplyRun and verify changes

Run deployments from the repository root. deploy.py initializes shared state and includes task modules according to the selected host's configuration and available secrets.

docs.title: Before the first deployment
docs.text:
1. Read the safety notes in the README.
  2. Review inventory.py; verify target names, SSH hostnames, ports, users and _sudo settings.
  3. Review the matching group_data/<host>.py and every group-data file for groups assigned to that target. Remove example settings that do not belong on the target. For example, @local belongs to the workstation group in the supplied inventory and therefore receives group_data/workstation.py.
  4. Prepare secrets.json.gpg only if the enabled features need secrets. Use gpg-vault create or gpg-vault edit after the script has been deployed; see Secrets management.
  5. Confirm SSH connectivity and privilege escalation on remote targets.
  6. Back up important system and application configuration, and arrange console/out-of-band access for firewall or network changes.

docs.title: Preview and apply
docs.text:
# Show the planned changes without applying them
pyinfra inventory.py deploy.py --dry --diff

# Apply the deployment
pyinfra inventory.py deploy.py --diff

Limit execution to one host when testing:

pyinfra inventory.py deploy.py --limit @local --dry --diff

The precise CLI options can vary with pyinfra versions; consult pyinfra --help if an option is unavailable. --diff helps inspect file changes. A dry run is not a substitute for reviewing task code, backups, or recovery access.

docs.title: Core tasks
docs.text:
These modules are always included by deploy.py:

  1. tasks/apt.py
  2. tasks/hosts.py
  3. tasks/sudo.py
  4. tasks/system.py
  5. tasks/ssh_keys.py
  6. tasks/git.py
  7. tasks/fonts.py
  8. tasks/scripts.py
  9. tasks/mc.py

The core set can still have conditional behavior internally, but its modules are included on every deployment. tasks/scripts.py also deploys the gpg-vault utility from files/scripts/ and creates its command link. The complete inclusion matrix, including cron, Samba, Docker lifecycle and nested workstation gates, is in the Feature reference.

docs.title: Optional tasks
docs.text:
The optional modules are included only when the relevant configuration and runtime prerequisites are satisfied. The full inclusion matrix is maintained in the Feature reference.

Feature Inclusion condition Module(s) Cron Non-empty cron_jobs tasks/cron.py Flatpak Flatpak executable detected during initialization tasks/flatpak.py SSH client Truthy ssh_config tasks/ssh_config.py WireGuard config Truthy wireguard_config and secrets.wireguard; wireguard_enabled defaults true tasks/wireguard.py VPN activation local_network_cidr and wireguard_interface; vpn_enabled defaults true tasks/vpn.py Syncthing Truthy syncthing; nested enabled defaults true tasks/syncthing.py Shell/terminal Truthy zsh, tmux or powerline respectively tasks/zsh.py, tasks/tmux.py, tasks/powerline.py Samba Truthy samba; nested enabled defaults false tasks/samba.py UFW Truthy ufw; nested enabled defaults true tasks/ufw.py Docker Truthy docker tasks/docker.py, tasks/docker_container.py Docker battery monitor Docker enabled; docker_power_monitor defaults true tasks/docker_power.py Sablier Docker enabled and docker_sablier.enabled true tasks/docker_sablier.py Caddy/certificates Docker enabled, truthy caddy_config, and caddy_enabled defaults true tasks/caddy.py, tasks/dehydrated.py AppArmor Truthy apparmor_profiles; apparmor_enabled defaults true tasks/apparmor.py Mullvad extensions Truthy mullvad_extensions; mullvad_browser_enabled defaults true tasks/mullvad_extensions.py VSCodium extensions Truthy vscodium; vscodium_enabled defaults true tasks/vscodium.py Proton applications Truthy proton tasks/proton.py

Docker service dispatch is configuration-key based. Supported application keys include adguard_home, appflowy, firefly-iii, forgejo, grav, homepage, linkwarden, mdmesh, miniflux, nocodb, paperless, portainer, snipe-it, tasmoadmin, timetagger, vaultwarden, wallabag and wg-easy. See Docker services and the Feature reference for the application catalog.

Sablier and the Docker battery monitor are mutually exclusive. When Sablier is enabled, the battery monitor is disabled and containers it previously stopped are restored. Caddy's Dehydrated DNS-01 flow requires secrets.dehydrated.hetzner_api_token.

docs.title: Workstation role tasks
docs.text:
The workstation role is assigned through inventory group membership, not by naming a host workstation. In the supplied inventory, workstation = ["@local"] assigns the local target to the group; its shared settings are in group_data/workstation.py.

deploy.py checks these nested workstation flags and includes the matching module only when enabled is true:

Setting Module Notes workstation.backup.enabled tasks/workstation/backup.py Installs backup tools and renders Borgmatic configuration; does not schedule or run backups. workstation.power.enabled tasks/workstation/power.py Installs/enables either TLP or Power Profiles Daemon and removes the conflicting manager. workstation.hardware.enabled tasks/workstation/hardware.py Installs fwupd and optional Intel/AMD microcode; no unattended firmware updates. workstation.storage.enabled tasks/workstation/storage.py Installs SMART/NVMe inspection tools; no polling or alert schedule. workstation.peripherals.enabled tasks/workstation/peripherals.py Printer and scanner packages are separately controlled by printing and scanning; printing enables CUPS. workstation.desktop.enabled tasks/workstation/desktop.py Installs common desktop integration packages; optional packages replaces the defaults. workstation.maintenance.enabled tasks/workstation/maintenance.py Installs maintenance utilities only; no unattended upgrades or scheduled reboots. workstation.cosmic.enabled tasks/workstation/cosmic/deploy.py Applies independently enabled appearance, window management, input, shortcuts, panel, dock, workspaces and optional config-file synchronization. Display/output settings are not managed. workstation.limusic.enabled tasks/workstation/limusic.py Installs the latest stable x86-64 AppImage after SHA-256 verification and creates a desktop launcher. workstation.limusic.enabled tasks/workstation/limusic.py Installs the stable x86-64 AppImage after SHA-256 verification and creates its desktop launcher.

The tracked workstation example disables all workstation features by default. Audit and explicitly enable each feature before applying a deployment.

docs.title: Deployment behavior to understand
docs.text:
For the full top-level host-data index, optional task gates, COSMIC subfeatures, Docker application catalog and every task module, see the Complete feature and configuration reference.

  • tasks/apt.py configures configured repositories, refreshes package indexes, upgrades packages when the index update changes, and installs configured packages.
  • tasks/system.py can change hostname, timezone, locale, editor environment, keyboard layout, sysctl, udev and USBGuard configuration.
  • tasks/ufw.py sets default incoming traffic to deny and outgoing traffic to allow, applies supported application/port rules, then enables UFW. Supported keys are chromecast-dlna, kdeconnect, localsend and ssh; each accepts Allow or Deny, while unknown keys/values are ignored. Explicitly allow the actual remote-management port before deployment: the checked-in local example sets ssh to Deny, which can cut off remote access.
  • tasks/ssh_keys.py does not overwrite existing private keys, but can manage authorized keys.
  • tasks/wireguard.py installs WireGuard and writes interface configuration; it does not start or enable the service.
  • tasks/vpn.py enables and starts wg-quick@<interface> when no globally scoped IPv4 address belongs to local_network_cidr. It only examines IPv4 addresses.
  • Docker tasks prepare Compose projects with docker compose up --no-start so Sablier can start services on demand. A changed Compose file triggers an image pull and service reconciliation; user-level systemd operations run as the configured account (or via runuser when deployment runs as root). Sablier's default dynamic strategy serves a themed loading page while a service starts; blocking mode is available for clients that cannot use the dynamic page. See Task reference.

docs.title: Recommended operating loop
docs.text:
1. Make one focused configuration change.
  2. Run a dry deployment against one host.
  3. Inspect the diff and the task implementation for high-impact operations.
  4. Apply to the test host.
  5. Verify the resulting service, network, access and application behavior.
  6. Expand to additional hosts only after validation.

For task-level detail, see Task reference. For implementation work, see Development.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
BUILD AND VALIDATE SAFELY

Set up the development environment, run the project checks and follow the conventions used when extending pyinfra tasks.

uvReproducible environment pytestTask regression coverage pre-commitLint and quality checks

This guide covers local development, validation and the conventions used when extending the automation.

docs.title: Development environment
docs.text:
The project requires Python 3.12 or newer. Runtime dependencies are declared in pyproject.toml and mirrored in requirements.txt; development tools are in the dev dependency group. uv.lock is intentionally ignored by Git and is generated locally by uv, so it is not a repository-pinned lockfile.

Install uv if it is not already available, then synchronize the environment:

uv sync --dev
pre-commit install

Activate the created virtual environment when running commands interactively:

source .venv/bin/activate

After changing dependencies in pyproject.toml, run uv lock and uv sync --dev to refresh the local environment. When adding or changing runtime dependencies, also update requirements.txt, because deployment environments install from that file. Prefer uv add PACKAGE for runtime dependencies and uv add --dev PACKAGE for development dependencies.

docs.title: Makefile shortcuts
docs.text:
The repository root includes a Makefile for common development and deployment commands. Run make help to list the targets.

Target Purpose make sync Run uv sync --dev. make hooks Install the pre-commit Git hooks. make lint Run all pre-commit hooks against tracked files. make test Run the pytest suite. make compile Check Python and shell syntax, to check syntax. make check Run lint, tests and syntax checks. make dry-run Preview deployment with --dry --diff. make deploy Apply the deployment with --diff.

Deployment targets are deliberately limited to @local by default. Select another target explicitly, for example:

make dry-run TARGET_ARGS="--limit hostname"
make deploy TARGET_ARGS="--limit hostname"

You can also override INVENTORY, DEPLOY, UV, PYTHON, PYTEST, PRE_COMMIT or PYINFRA when using a different executable or deployment entry point. Review the preview before running make deploy; the Makefile does not replace the deployment safety checks described below.

docs.title: Run checks
docs.text:
Run all configured hooks:

pre-commit run --all-files

Run one hook:

pre-commit run pylint --all-files
pre-commit run check-yaml --all-files
pre-commit run check-json --all-files

The source of truth for hook versions and arguments is .pre-commit-config.yaml.

docs.title: Run the test suite
docs.text:
Run the mocked task regression tests in the synchronized development environment:

uv run pytest tests/ -v

The tests stub pyinfra host, fact and operation APIs. They check task-module evaluation and selected helper behavior without connecting to or changing a real host. Run these checks locally before submitting a pull request. GitHub Actions also runs pytest, pre-commit and strict MkDocs validation on pull requests and changes to main; none of these checks deploy to a host.

Check the documentation site with mkdocs build --strict (after installing MkDocs Material). Publishing to GitHub Pages is manual only: open the repository's Actions tab, select Publish GitHub Pages, and click Run workflow. The publishing job checks out main, builds the site with mkdocs build --strict, and updates the gh-pages branch. There is no publication on push or pull request. For local desktop application builds, see Pyinfra Manager.

The coverage inventory in .github/ci/task_coverage.json enumerates every Python task module and every file under files/scripts/. The tests/test_task_coverage.py checks that the inventory cannot silently omit new or removed files, that every task module is explicitly classified, and that Python and shell utility sources pass syntax validation. It also evaluates every deployment module in a mocked pyinfra context with safe fixtures and requires each module to schedule at least one operation; dispatchers must include at least one child task. The helper classification is reserved for shared code that does not itself schedule pyinfra operations. These module smoke tests validate deployment preparation and operation scheduling, not changes on a live host. Use a disposable target for any real deployment validation. A separate behavioral coverage map in tests/function_coverage.json links every Python function in tasks/ and files/scripts/ to one or more pytest cases. tests/test_function_coverage.py compares that map against the AST-discovered function inventory and verifies that mapped tests exist and assert results or expected exceptions. Keep the map synchronized when adding, removing or renaming functions. The mapping is an inventory guard, not a substitute for reviewing whether each test asserts the function's expected outputs, side effects and no-op behavior.

docs.title: Deployment validation
docs.text: The project does not run automated deployment checks. For infrastructure changes, validate task behavior with the mocked pytest suite, then review a pyinfra dry run against a disposable or otherwise recoverable target before applying changes. A second deployment against an already-converged target should report no changes. Do not use production hosts as test targets.

docs.title: Configured checks
docs.text:
Check Purpose check-added-large-files Rejects newly added files over the configured size limit (2000 KB). check-yaml Validates YAML syntax. check-json Validates JSON syntax. pretty-format-json / jsonlint Formats JSON using the configured hook arguments. trailing-whitespace Removes trailing whitespace. end-of-file-fixer Ensures a final newline. check-merge-conflict Detects unresolved merge markers. pylint Lints Python files with the configured disabled-message list. yamllint Lints YAML in strict mode.

Some hooks modify files automatically. Review the resulting diff after running them.

docs.title: Adding a feature
docs.text:
1. Identify whether the feature belongs to one host or a reusable inventory group/role. Put host-specific settings in group_data/<host>.py; put shared role settings in group_data/<group>.py and assign hosts to that group in inventory.py.
  2. Add or update a focused task module under tasks/ (use a subdirectory such as tasks/workstation/ for a cohesive role).
  3. Add static payloads to files/ or parameterized Jinja2 templates to templates/.
  4. Add the task inclusion condition to deploy.py if it is optional. For grouped roles, gate each task on a nested role feature setting (for example, host.data.get("workstation", {}).get("backup", {}).get("enabled", False)).
  5. Keep credentials in the encrypted secrets document and update secrets.json.gpg.example with placeholders when the schema changes. files/scripts/gpg-vault is the interactive workflow for maintaining that encrypted file; keep its command help and Secrets management documentation in sync when changing it.
  6. Document configuration keys, prerequisites, side effects and recovery considerations.
  7. Run pre-commit and test a dry run against a disposable or non-production target.

docs.title: Task design conventions
docs.text:
• Keep each task focused on one system concern or service.
  • Prefer host.data.get("key", default) for optional configuration.
  • Validate externally supplied values before constructing operations.
  • Use pyinfra facts and conditional operations to avoid unnecessary changes.
  • host.get_fact(Command, ...) returns a list of output lines, not a string. Use common.command_output_text() before applying string methods or comparing complete command output.
  • Do not branch on an operation's .changed state during task preparation. Use OperationMeta.did_change callbacks or any_changed() in _if conditions so dependent operations are evaluated during execution.
  • Make ownership, group and permissions explicit for sensitive files.
  • Avoid overwriting existing private keys or user data unless explicitly intended.
  • Handle service reloads/restarts only when the relevant configuration changes.
  • Never log private keys, passwords, tokens or full credential URLs.

docs.title: Documentation conventions
docs.text:
• Use relative links between documents in this repository.
  • Include runnable examples, but use reserved/example values rather than real host details.
  • Distinguish task inclusion conditions from settings consumed inside a task.
  • Document whether a task installs software, writes configuration, starts services or changes firewall/network state.
  • Update the README and the relevant docs/ reference when behavior changes.

docs.title: Pull request checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Configuration defaults and feature gates match the implementation.
  • [ ] No real credentials, private keys, host-specific identifiers or personal data were added.
  • [ ] Operations have been reviewed for privilege, destructive effects and remote lockout risk.
  • [ ] Dry-run output has been reviewed on a suitable target.
  • [ ] pre-commit run --all-files passes.
  • [ ] uv run pytest tests/ -v passes.
  • [ ] README and relevant documentation have been updated.

See CONTRIBUTING.md for repository contribution guidance.

The tmux task schedules plugin installation and updates as pyinfra operations after the tmux-plugin-manager package operation. It verifies both plugin-manager scripts at execution time and only runs plugin management when the package or tmux configuration changes. This avoids invoking commands during deployment preparation, before queued package installation has executed, and avoids reporting changes on an unchanged second deployment.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text: This repository publishes GitHub Releases from semantic-version tags; it is not packaged for PyPI. Follow the release guide to prepare the changelog, tag a release commit and publish the generated release notes.

docs.title: Docker services
docs.text:
Deploy and operate containerized applications with a shared Compose and systemd workflow. Each service is opt-in through host.data.docker; persistent state lives in the configured user's home directory.
