docs.title: Workstation role tasks
docs.text:
The modules below are included by deploy.py only when the matching nested setting under host.data.workstation has enabled: True. Their shared defaults are defined in group_data/workstation.py; inventory membership determines which hosts receive that group data.

Module Responsibility Configuration tasks/workstation/backup.py Installs Restic, Borg, rsync and Borgmatic; renders /etc/borgmatic/config.yaml. It does not create, schedule or run backups. workstation.backup.enabled tasks/workstation/power.py Installs/enables TLP or Power Profiles Daemon and removes the conflicting manager. workstation.power.enabled, workstation.power.manager tasks/workstation/hardware.py Installs fwupd and optional CPU microcode. Firmware updates are not applied automatically. workstation.hardware.enabled, workstation.hardware.cpu_vendor (intel, amd or unset) tasks/workstation/storage.py Installs smartmontools and nvme-cli; does not configure polling or alerting. workstation.storage.enabled tasks/workstation/peripherals.py Installs optional printer/scanner packages; enables CUPS when printing is selected. workstation.peripherals.enabled, printing, scanning tasks/workstation/desktop.py Installs common desktop integration utilities. A custom package list replaces the defaults. workstation.desktop.enabled, optional packages list tasks/workstation/maintenance.py Installs needrestart, debian-goodies and apt-file; does not enable unattended upgrades or schedule reboots. workstation.maintenance.enabled tasks/workstation/limusic.py Installs the latest stable Limusic x86-64 AppImage, verifies its published SHA-256 digest, deploys the matching upstream icon and creates a user-level desktop launcher discoverable by COSMIC. The AppImage retains its self-updater. workstation.limusic.enabled

The tracked group_data/workstation.py.example disables every workstation feature by default. Copy it to the ignored group_data/workstation.py and explicitly enable the features required by each host. Review the group data before assigning additional hosts to the workstation group. Limusic is also disabled by default; set workstation.limusic.enabled = True to install it for the configured user. The task uses the latest stable x86-64 AppImage from Limusic releases, checks the release-published SHA-256 digest, installs the matching application icon under ~/.local/share/icons/, and writes ~/.local/share/applications/limusic.desktop so COSMIC can find it. The AppImage is stored in ~/.local/opt/limusic/ and keeps Limusic's built-in updater; the task downloads a new stable release only when the release tag changes.

docs.title: Cron jobs
docs.text:
Define jobs in the host or group data key cron_jobs. The list is empty by default, so hosts without configured jobs do not install or enable cron. Each entry requires a stable name, a single-line command, and at least one schedule field (minute, hour, day_of_month, month, day_of_week, or special_time). The schedule fields accept the same values as pyinfra's crontab.crontab operation, including lists and cron expressions such as "*/15".

  • scope: "user" (default) manages the crontab of the configured username.
  • scope: "root" manages root's crontab.
  • present: False removes the named job; keep its name and command in the configuration while removing it.
  • The stable name is stored as pyinfra's cron_name, so changing a command or schedule updates the existing entry instead of adding a duplicate.
  • The task installs the Debian/Ubuntu cron package and ensures the cron service is enabled and running whenever the list contains jobs. Both scopes are managed through sudo, so the deployment account needs suitable sudo privileges.
  • Duplicate names within the same target user's crontab, multiline names/commands and unknown configuration fields are rejected.

Example:

cron_jobs = [
    {
        "name": "daily-cleanup",
        "command": "/usr/local/bin/cleanup.sh",
        "scope": "user",
        "special_time": "@daily",
    },
    {
        "name": "system-maintenance",
        "command": "/usr/local/sbin/maintenance.sh",
        "scope": "root",
        "minute": 0,
        "hour": 4,
    },
]

docs.title: Linkwarden bookmarks in Homepage
docs.text: When both docker.linkwarden and docker.homepage are configured and secrets.docker.homepage.environment.HOMEPAGE_VAR_LINKWARDEN_API_KEY is present, tasks/docker/linkwarden_bookmarks.py runs on the pyinfra controller before Homepage is rendered. It retrieves the authenticated account’s paginated Linkwarden search results, groups URL bookmarks by collection, and updates only the marked managed section in group_data/@local.py. Favicons are stored in files/homepage/icons/ and deployed by the existing additive Homepage icon sync. Manual bookmarks outside the managed section are preserved. Run python tasks/docker/linkwarden_bookmarks.py --dry-run from the repository checkout to preview the generated groups; this fetches the API data but does not download favicons or modify files. Run the same command without --dry-run to perform the synchronization manually. API or pagination failures abort synchronization before the managed bookmarks are changed; unavailable favicons are simply omitted. The controller therefore needs network access to the configured Linkwarden domain and write access to the repository checkout. Reuse the existing Homepage Linkwarden widget API key from the encrypted secrets file; no additional token is needed. Configure docker.linkwarden.blacklist in group_data/@local.py with Linkwarden bookmark IDs (integers or strings) to omit selected bookmarks. IDs are matched against each API result’s id field; URLs are never used as blacklist keys. The default empty list synchronizes all eligible bookmarks. Remove an ID from the list to restore that bookmark on the next run.

docs.title: GPG secret utility
docs.text: tasks/scripts.py deploys files/scripts/gpg-vault with the other user scripts and creates its command link. The helper provides create, edit, view, encrypt, decrypt, rekey and status; see Secrets management. It is not invoked by deploy.py: common.initialize() remains responsible for decrypting secrets.json.gpg during deployment.

docs.title: UFW firewall
docs.text: tasks/ufw.py supports the chromecast-dlna, kdeconnect and localsend application profiles plus ssh (TCP port 22). These entries accept Allow or Deny string values. Additional custom rules use a dictionary with an action and a rule string containing UFW arguments. Existing custom rules are read from ufw show added and compared before changes, including normalization of the optional in token, to keep deployments idempotent. Invalid entries are ignored. The task sets default incoming policy to deny and outgoing policy to allow, applies configured rules, and then enables UFW. Review firewall changes and ensure a recovery path before applying them remotely; the supplied local configuration sets ssh to Deny.

docs.title: APT
docs.text: Repository definitions include a signing-key URL and destination plus repository URL, distribution, components and optional architectures/types. Review third-party repository configuration carefully: adding a repository delegates package trust to that repository's signing key and publishing process.

docs.title: SSH keys and client hardening
docs.text:
The key task supports Ed25519 and RSA key generation; RSA keys must be at least 3072 bits. Private keys are not overwritten when they already exist. Passphrases can be supplied through secrets.ssh. Keep backups of keys and verify authorized-key changes before removing access paths.

The SSH client task writes a global Host * baseline before the configured ssh_config host entries. It enables HashKnownHosts, StrictHostKeyChecking accept-new, UpdateHostKeys, and public-key authentication; disables agent forwarding, X11 forwarding, local commands and configured forwarding; and sets connection timeout/keepalive values. With OpenSSH's first-obtained-value behavior, these baseline options take precedence over later host-specific entries. accept-new automatically records previously unseen host keys but still rejects changed keys; verify host fingerprints through a trusted channel when onboarding sensitive systems.

docs.title: WireGuard and VPN activation
docs.text: The WireGuard task installs the package and renders one file per configured interface. The VPN task is separate: it uses pyinfra's hardware.Ipv4Addrs fact, excludes loopback, link-local and unspecified addresses to match globally scoped IPv4 detection, compares the remaining addresses with local_network_cidr, and enables/runs the configured wg-quick@... service when outside that network. IPv6 is not considered by the network-detection check.

docs.title: Docker services
docs.text:
Docker is an optional feature enabled by a truthy docker mapping in host data. tasks/docker.py installs Docker and defines the shared Compose/systemd helper; tasks/docker_container.py dispatches each configured service module.

The deployment helper renders Compose projects below ~/.docker/<service>/ and user-level systemd units below ~/.config/systemd/user/. Changed Compose files trigger image pulls and service reconciliation; unchanged files do not trigger pulls. Additional generated assets can register precise restart triggers. Sablier changes preparation to docker compose up --no-start and starts labelled applications on demand.

All persistent service data uses direct host-directory bind mounts below ~/.docker/; Docker-managed named volumes are not used. See the dedicated Docker services guide for the service catalog, ports, storage paths, lifecycle, security and service-specific configuration notes.

docs.title: Browser and editor extensions
docs.text: Mullvad extension downloads are defined by extension IDs and URLs. The supplied local configuration includes Wallabagger for connecting the browser to the self-hosted Wallabag instance. VSCodium extension installation is additive: already-installed extensions are detected and left in place. Review external download sources before enabling either task.

docs.title: Proton
docs.text: The Proton task supports components selected through the proton configuration, including Mail, Mail Bridge, VPN, Pass and Drive CLI. Installation source varies by component and configuration; consult tasks/proton.py for the exact current options. When Drive CLI installation is enabled, set proton.drive_cli_version explicitly; deployment fails if it is missing or empty. The deprecated misspelled proton.drive_cll_version setting is no longer accepted.

docs.title: On-demand Samba file exchange
docs.text: tasks/samba.py | samba.enabled | Installs Samba with guest Upload and read-only Download shares, but leaves smbd stopped and masked. The samba-start and samba-stop scripts manage TCP 445 UFW rules and service lifecycle. Optional samba.idle_timeout enables automatic shutdown after a period without SMB traffic. See Samba configuration and security.

docs.title: Run an individual task
docs.text:
For diagnosis or focused testing, pyinfra can run a task file directly. Example:

pyinfra inventory.py tasks/system.py --dry --diff

A task run directly may not have all initialization or feature-gate behavior of deploy.py; inspect whether the task initializes shared state itself. Prefer the full entry point for normal provisioning.

docs.title: On-demand Docker services
docs.text:
On-demand startup is controlled by docker_sablier. The tracked group_data/@local.py.example disables Sablier by default and documents a 15-minute default session for when it is enabled. Browser-facing routes use Sablier's dynamic strategy by default: while an idle service resumes or starts, Sablier immediately serves a themed loading page that periodically checks readiness and then redirects the browser to the requested URL. The default theme is ghost, details are shown, and the page refreshes every five seconds. Dynamic mode avoids holding the original browser request open, so Caddy no longer has a global two-minute response write deadline. Only Caddy reverse-proxy routes whose loopback port matches a configured Docker service are wrapped; unmatched routes remain unchanged.

Sablier runs as a Docker container using its Docker provider and the Docker socket. Caddy runs in a custom Docker image containing the Sablier Caddy plugin. Caddy uses host networking so existing loopback reverse-proxy upstreams continue to work. Dehydrated runs inside the Caddy container and uses the Hetzner DNS-01 hook; set secrets.dehydrated.hetzner_api_token in the encrypted secrets file.

Each Compose workload is prepared with docker compose up --no-start. This creates missing containers and reconciles changed Compose configuration (including Sablier labels) without starting on-demand services. Existing container labels are checked against the generated override; label drift forces a Compose recreation and restarts the user systemd unit so the workload is brought back up with the corrected labels. This is required because Docker container labels are immutable after creation. Sablier resumes a paused or starts a stopped labelled application container when a matching request arrives. Sablier follows Compose depends_on metadata to start required dependencies in order. Dependencies that should share the application's idle lifecycle must also carry sablier.enable=true and the same group.

The sablier_services list under a service's docker.<service> configuration declares every Compose service to pause or stop together when its session expires. It defaults to app_services, so dependencies remain running unless explicitly included. One-shot containers must not be included. Add database and supporting service names when they should share the application's idle-session lifecycle.

The separate app_services list identifies application containers for systemd stop behavior. stop_dependencies controls whether manually stopping the user systemd unit stops the complete Compose project or only those application containers; it does not control Sablier's idle-session behavior.

Per-service overrides remain available under docker.<service>.sablier. Supported options include enabled, group, session_duration, strategy, display_name, theme, show_details and refresh_frequency. The global defaults are strategy: dynamic, theme: ghost, show_details: True and refresh_frequency: 5s. Set enabled: False to keep a service outside Sablier management. Use strategy: blocking for clients that cannot handle the dynamic HTML waiting page; blocking_timeout remains configurable globally and per service for that strategy. Homepage is managed by Sablier by default; only its configured widget API paths bypass Sablier so dashboard widgets can retrieve data without waking the target services.

Caddy performs the initial Dehydrated run before starting its server. A user-level systemd timer runs daily at 03:00 and invokes the renewal script inside the container with docker exec; Persistent=true catches a missed run after downtime. The script reloads Caddy only when certificate fingerprints change. The image creates the /etc/dehydrated/conf.d directory configured by CONFIG_D, and the Hetzner hook safely handles both numeric and textual exit_hook arguments. The Caddy Compose service has a health check against its local admin API, and pyinfra waits for it to become healthy after a recreation. After the health check, pyinfra compares the deployed Caddyfile checksum with a marker stored in the persistent /config bind mount. A missing or mismatched marker triggers Caddyfile validation and a reload; the marker is updated atomically only after both commands succeed. This makes a skipped or failed reload retry on the next deployment even when the template itself reports no change, while an unchanged acknowledged configuration avoids unnecessary reloads. A newly started Caddy container reads its mounted Caddyfile at startup. Pyinfra checks each preceding file operation's did_change() result before enabling the renewal-timer, image-build, container-start or health-wait operation; an unchanged, present image and healthy container do not trigger these operations.

Caddy's entrypoint starts with the minimal NET_BIND_SERVICE, SETUID and SETGID capabilities, runs Dehydrated at startup and on its daily timer as the configured deployment user, then starts Caddy as that same non-root user with only the ambient NET_BIND_SERVICE capability needed for ports 80 and 443. The Compose service drops all other capabilities and keeps no-new-privileges enabled. Caddy's persistent configuration, Dehydrated state, certificates, data and runtime state use explicit host bind mounts from directories below ~/.docker/caddy/. Sablier and Caddy are deployed only when Docker and their corresponding configuration gates are enabled. Existing host Caddy installations are not migrated, stopped, or uninstalled automatically; prepare ports 80 and 443 manually before enabling the Docker-based Caddy service.

Sablier and the Docker battery saver are mutually exclusive. The global docker_sablier.provider_strategy defaults to pause: idle containers are frozen and resume quickly on the next request, but continue consuming RAM. Set it to stop to release their memory at the cost of a cold start. Sablier applies this strategy to every managed Docker container; it cannot select pause or stop per service. Sablier 1.20.0 has no built-in delayed stop after a pause, so a one-hour pause-then-stop lifecycle is not configured here. When Sablier is enabled, the battery monitor is stopped and disabled, and containers previously stopped by the battery saver are restored first. Disabling Sablier re-enables the battery monitor.

docs.title: Templates and static assets
docs.text:
GENERATE CONFIGURATION CONSISTENTLY

Use Jinja2 templates to render host-aware configuration files while keeping reusable content separate from task execution.

Jinja2Render dynamic values Host dataSupply per-machine settings TasksDeploy only changed output

Task modules use two asset types:

  • Templates in templates/ are rendered with host-specific values or secrets.
  • Static files in files/ are copied or synchronized without Jinja2 rendering.

The consuming task controls the destination, owner, group, permissions and any service reload/restart behavior.

docs.title: Jinja2 templates
docs.text:
Template Consumer Purpose templates/apt_repository.list.j2 tasks/apt.py APT source-list entries. templates/ssh_config.j2 tasks/ssh_config.py User SSH client configuration. templates/wireguard.conf.j2 tasks/wireguard.py WireGuard interface configuration. templates/dehydrated_config.j2 tasks/dehydrated.py dehydrated configuration. templates/workstation/borgmatic.yml.j2 tasks/workstation/backup.py Borgmatic configuration deployed to /etc/borgmatic/config.yaml. templates/Caddyfile.j2 tasks/caddy.py Caddy site configuration. templates/docker/* Docker task modules Service-specific Compose definitions and the shared user-level systemd service unit. templates/git/* tasks/git.py Git credentials/configuration fragments. templates/dotfiles/* User environment tasks Rendered user dotfiles.

Templates may receive host data, runtime values initialized by common.py, and explicit keyword arguments from the calling task. Do not assume every template has access to every variable: inspect the call site to determine the actual context.

docs.title: Docker Compose templates and persistent data
docs.text:
Each service has a Compose template under templates/docker/<service>/docker-compose.yml.j2; the shared systemd unit is templates/docker/systemd.service.j2. Compose files are deployed to ~/.docker/<service>/docker-compose.yml. Persistent data is stored in host directories under ~/.docker/ and mounted into the containers:

Service Host path Container path Miniflux PostgreSQL ~/.docker/miniflux/db/ /var/lib/postgresql/data TimeTagger ~/.docker/timetagger/ /root/_timetagger Grav ~/.docker/grav/data/ /var/www/html Forgejo ~/.docker/forgejo/data/ /data Portainer ~/.docker/portainer/data/ /data TasmoAdmin ~/.docker/tasmoadmin/data/ /data/tasmoadmin Wallabag data ~/.docker/wallabag/data/ /var/www/wallabag/data Wallabag images ~/.docker/wallabag/images/ /var/www/wallabag/web/assets/images Vaultwarden ~/.docker/vaultwarden/ /data NocoDB ~/.docker/nocodb/data/ /usr/app/data Homepage ~/.docker/homepage/config/ plus public/icons/ and public/images/ /app/config, /app/public/icons, /app/public/images Linkwarden ~/.docker/linkwarden/postgres/, data/, meili/ PostgreSQL, application data, Meilisearch data Paperless-ngx ~/.docker/paperless/postgres/, data/, media/, consume/, export/ PostgreSQL and Paperless data directories Firefly III ~/.docker/firefly-iii/database/, upload/, fints/ MariaDB, uploads and importer config Snipe-IT ~/.docker/snipe-it/database/, storage/ MariaDB and /var/lib/snipeit WG-Easy ~/.docker/wg-easy/ /etc/wireguard and application data

All configured service data mounts use direct host bind mounts; Compose does not create Docker-managed named volumes. The task creates service configuration directories, but the service modules may also create or assign ownership to application data directories where required. Review the individual Compose template and task before changing mount paths: application UID/GID requirements differ between images.

Some older service templates used Docker-managed named volumes. Switching an existing deployment from a named-volume layout to the current host bind mounts does not copy existing volume contents; migrate the data explicitly before applying the change.

docs.title: Important generated destinations
docs.text:
Asset Destination / behavior SSH client configuration ~/.ssh/config, restrictive mode 0600. WireGuard interface /etc/wireguard/<interface>.conf, owned by root with mode 0640. The task does not start the interface. dehydrated config /etc/dehydrated/config, root-owned with mode 0600. Borgmatic config /etc/borgmatic/config.yaml, root-owned with mode 0600; review and complete its repository/source settings before relying on it. The current template also contains the literal fallback passphrase B0rgm4t1C!—do not use that default for real backups. dehydrated hook /etc/dehydrated/hook.sh, root-owned with executable permissions. Docker Compose ~/.docker/<service>/ under the configured user's home. Docker systemd unit ~/.config/systemd/user/<service>.service. Git credentials ~/.git-credentials, mode 0600, only when matching secrets exist. User scripts ~/scripts/; symlinks are created in /usr/local/bin/.

Borgmatic passphrase warning: templates/workstation/borgmatic.yml.j2 renders encryption_passphrase from borg_passphrase or the literal fallback B0rgm4t1C!. tasks/workstation/backup.py currently does not pass borg_passphrase explicitly, so the fallback is used by the current task. The generated config is root-owned with mode 0600, which protects it from unprivileged local users, but the fallback is public in source and is not suitable for a real repository. Do not initialize or rely on a production Borg repository with this fallback; replace it with a unique secret and verify the rendering path before use.

Exact paths can be service- or task-specific and should be confirmed in the implementation before changing them.

docs.title: Adding an asset
docs.text:
1. Place the file under a directory that reflects its consumer or feature.
  2. Reference it from the relevant task using a repository-relative path.
  3. Set destination, owner, group and mode explicitly.
  4. Consider whether a changed file requires a daemon reload, service restart or cache refresh.
  5. Ensure secrets are not rendered into world-readable files or exposed in logs.
  6. Update this reference and the relevant task/configuration documentation.

docs.title: Project relationship
docs.text:
pyinfra is an open-source infrastructure automation tool maintained separately in the pyinfra-dev/pyinfra repository.

This repository, gpkvt/pyinfra, contains deployment configuration built on that tool. It is not the upstream engine source tree and does not define upstream pyinfra behavior.

docs.title: Upstream concepts used here
docs.text:
• Inventory selects target hosts and organizes them into groups.
  • Host and group data supplies configuration values to deploy code.
  • Deploys compose Python code into a deployment.
  • Facts inspect the current state of target systems.
  • Operations describe changes to files, packages, services and other resources.
  • Connectors provide local and remote execution mechanisms.
  • Dry runs display the planned operations before execution.

The upstream documentation describes the supported interfaces and behavior in detail.
